verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and self-contained. In a partner step, reflection across the perpendicular bisector of AC exchanges A and C and sends D to E, so it preserves the four side lengths as a multiset and preserves the relevant sum of opposite interior angles; the complementary opposite-angle sum is then preserved because a convex quadrilateral has angle sum 2pi. For fixed cyclically ordered side lengths and a fixed opposite-angle sum, the cosine-law equation has at most one admissible value of the chosen angle because its two sides are strictly monotone in opposite directions. SAS rigidity and convexity then determine at most one congruence class for each ordered side-length quadruple. Since there are at most 4! such quadruples, any partner sequence has only finitely many congruence classes, ruling out an infinite pairwise noncongruent sequence. The proof uses no external references or internal fact IDs, and none of the hard prohibitions applies.
